newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria not actively seeking GiroCredit buyer.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria not actively seeking GiroCredit buyer.

text.p: Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa said on Sunday he would not actively look for buyers for the stake of the City of Vienna's Anteilsverwaltung Zentralsparkasse (AVZ) in savings bank GiroCredit AG.
"We are definitely not going to go around offering it on a silver platter," Randa, who is also a board member of AVZ, told a news conference.
AVZ is currently controlled by the Social Democrat-dominated City of Vienna and holds 56 percent of GiroCredit and 45 percent of Bank Austria.
Finance Minister Viktor Klima said earlier on Sunday AVZ's stake in GiroCredit must be sold immediately, as part of a deal struck by the government to prepare Bank Austria for eventual privatisation.
"I am waiting for interested parties to show up," said Randa.

According to the agreement the state's 19 percent stake in Bank Austria would be floated immediately, while the 45 percent stake held by the City of Vienna's AVZ foundation is to be cut to below 25 percent within five years.
AVZ must put 20 percent of its current stake in a fiduciary account immediately. Its total holding will be reduced to below 20 percent after another two years.

The reduction of AVZ's stake would be achieved through a series of capital increases in which the foundation would not take part, Klima told reporters after a marathon emergency meeting between coalition leaders in the early hours of Sunday.

The government on Sunday announced Bank Austria as the winner of the bid for flagship bank Creditanstalt. The two banks will have combined assets of about 1,300 billion schillings ($120 billion) and a joint staff of about 16,000, the bank said. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
